en.headline: Health officials urge measles precautions for travellers amid global outbreaks
en.dek: The Centre for Health Protection says Hong Kong has recorded nine measles cases this year, mostly imported, and advises checking vaccination status before travel.
body: The Centre for Health Protection of the Department of Health reminded residents planning overseas travel to take precautions against measles, citing ongoing outbreaks in multiple countries linked to low vaccination rates.

Controller of the Centre for Health Protection Dr Edwin Tsui said the two-dose measles vaccination coverage in Hong Kong has remained consistently above 95 per cent according to school and territory-wide surveys, and most residents have immunity. He noted the risk of a large-scale local outbreak is relatively low, but Hong Kong faces importation risks as an international travel hub. A small number of people who have not completed vaccination, including some non-local born residents, foreign domestic helpers, overseas employees and students, could become infected and spread the virus to others without immunity, such as infants under one year old.

Hong Kong has recorded nine measles cases so far this year, of which six were imported or epidemiologically linked to imported cases involving travel to Indonesia, Pakistan and Vietnam during the incubation period, while three were local. In the United States more than 4,800 cases have been recorded this year, more than double last year’s total, with measles-related deaths in Pennsylvania and New York among unvaccinated people. Outbreaks have also occurred in Indonesia, Bangladesh, Laos and the Philippines.

People born before 1967 are considered immune through natural infection. Those born in or after 1967 who have not completed two doses of measles vaccine or whose vaccination history is unclear should consult a doctor to complete vaccination. Travellers to high-incidence areas who are unsure of their status should seek vaccination at least two weeks before departure. Pregnant women, women planning pregnancy and children under one without immunity are advised not to travel to outbreak areas. Students returning for winter holidays from affected countries should review their records and seek medical advice promptly if unwell, informing healthcare staff of symptoms and travel history.

zh.headline: 衛生防護中心籲外遊市民防麻疹 今年本港錄9宗個案
zh.dek: 中心指本港今年暫錄9宗麻疹，六宗與輸入有關，呼籲計劃外遊者出發前查閱目的地疫情並確保已接種兩劑疫苗。
body: 衛生署衛生防護中心提醒計劃外遊的市民採取適當預防措施，因全球多個地區因疫苗接種率偏低而持續出現麻疹疫情。
中心總監徐樂堅表示，根據小學學童接種覆蓋率及衛生署定期進行的全港免疫接種調查，兩劑麻疹疫苗的整體覆蓋率一直維持在95%以上，本地血清陽性率顯示大部分市民已有免疫力，大規模爆發風險相對偏低。然而香港作為國際旅遊頻繁的城市，仍面對輸入麻疹病毒的威脅。少數未完成接種的人士，包括部分非本地出生人士、外傭、海外僱員及來港升學人士，有機會受感染並傳播給未有免疫力的人士，例如一歲以下尚未接種第一劑疫苗的幼兒。
本港今年至今暫時錄9宗麻疹個案，其中6宗為外地輸入個案或與其有流行病學關連，病人潛伏期曾到過印尼、巴基斯坦和越南，其餘3宗為本地個案。美國今年已錄得超過4800宗個案，超過去年全年總數的兩倍，賓夕法尼亞州和紐約州出現麻疹相關死亡個案，死者均未接種疫苗。印尼、孟加拉、老撾和菲律賓亦出現爆發。

1967年前出生的市民可視為因自然感染而具備免疫力。1967年或以後出生而尚未完成兩劑接種或接種史不詳者，應盡快諮詢家庭醫生完成接種。計劃前往麻疹流行地區而從未或不確定曾接種兩劑者，應在出發前最少兩星期諮詢醫生。對麻疹沒有免疫力的懷孕婦女、計劃懷孕婦女及未滿一歲兒童不應前往爆發地區。身處受影響國家的留學生如不確定接種紀錄，應盡快安排接種；返港後如有不適，應立即求醫，並預先知會醫護人員病徵及旅遊史。
